absolut.explanation: "Absolut" means "absolutely" and makes a word stronger: Han har absolut ret (He is absolutely right). Det er absolut for sent (It is absolutely too late).

sentence.da: Det er **absolut** umuligt at nå toget nu.
sentence.en: It is absolutely impossible to catch the train now.

adgang.explanation: "Adgang" means "access" or "entry", the right to get in or to use something: Vi har ikke adgang til rummet (We do not have access to the room). Adgang forbudt (No entry) is a common sign.

sentence.da: Med dette kort får du **adgang** til hotellet.
sentence.en: With this card you get access to the hotel.

adopteret.explanation: "Adopteret" means "adopted", taken into a family as your own child: Hun er adopteret fra Kina (She is adopted from China). It comes from at adoptere (to adopt).

sentence.da: Hun er **adopteret** og kom til Danmark som baby.
sentence.en: She is adopted and came to Denmark as a baby.

af og til.explanation: "Af og til" means "now and then", for things that happen once in a while, not every day. Compare Jeg drikker kaffe hver dag (I drink coffee every day) with Jeg drikker kaffe af og til (I drink coffee now and then).

forms.da: jeg går i biografen af og til
forms.en: I go to the cinema now and then

sentence.da: Vi ses ikke ofte, kun **af og til**.
sentence.en: We do not see each other often, only now and then.

affald.explanation: "Affald" means "trash". You do not count it: Der er meget affald på gaden (There is a lot of trash on the street). One bag of it is en pose affald (a bag of trash).

sentence.da: Vi smider **affald** i skraldespanden.
sentence.en: We throw trash in the trash can.

afhængig.explanation: "Afhængig" means "dependent" or "addicted", and is used with af (of): Jeg er afhængig af kaffe (I am addicted to coffee). Det er afhængigt af vejret (It depends on the weather).

sentence.da: Min lillebror er **afhængig** af sin telefon.
sentence.en: My little brother is addicted to his phone.

aflyst.explanation: "Aflyst" means "canceled", for example a train, a flight or an event that will not take place. It is different from forsinket (delayed): a delayed train still comes, but a canceled one does not.

sentence.da: Toget er **aflyst** i dag.
sentence.en: The train is canceled today.

afrika.explanation: "Afrika" means "Africa". It is spelled with a k, not a c as in English. Add syd (south) to get Sydafrika (South Africa).

sentence.da: Løver og elefanter lever i **Afrika**.
sentence.en: Lions and elephants live in Africa.

afrikansk.explanation: "Afrikansk" means "African" and describes things from Africa: afrikansk musik (African music). For a person, use en afrikaner (an African).

sentence.da: Løven er et **afrikansk** dyr.
sentence.en: The lion is an African animal.

afslappet.explanation: "Afslappet" means "relaxed", for a person or a mood: Han er meget afslappet (He is very relaxed). Stemningen var afslappet (The mood was relaxed).

sentence.da: Efter ferien er jeg meget **afslappet**.
sentence.en: After the vacation, I am very relaxed.

afsted.explanation: "Afsted" means "off" or "away", for leaving a place. Compare Jeg er hjemme (I am at home) with Jeg skal afsted (I have to go / I am heading off). Han er afsted means "He has gone".

sentence.da: Hej hej, jeg skal **afsted** nu.
sentence.en: Bye bye, I have to go now.

aftensmad.explanation: "Aftensmad" means "dinner". It is built from aften (evening) and mad (food).

sentence.da: Om aftenen spiser vi **aftensmad** sammen.
sentence.en: In the evening we eat dinner together.

aggressiv.explanation: "Aggressiv" means "aggressive", ready to attack or shout: Han bliver aggressiv, når han er sur (He gets aggressive when he is grumpy). It is used for people, animals and words.

sentence.da: Hunden er **aggressiv** og viser tænderne.
sentence.en: The dog is aggressive and shows its teeth.

aktiv.explanation: "Aktiv" means "active", busy and doing things: Han er meget aktiv i klubben (He is very active in the club). It also means switched on: en aktiv konto (an active account).

sentence.da: Min bedstefar er stadig meget **aktiv** og går lange ture.
sentence.en: My grandfather is still very active and takes long walks.

al.explanation: "Al" means "all" and goes in front of an en-word you do not count: al musikken (all the music). For an et-word, use alt: alt vandet (all the water).

sentence.da: Jeg har spist **al** maden.
sentence.en: I have eaten all the food.

aldrig.explanation: "Aldrig" means "never". Compare Jeg drikker altid kaffe (I always drink coffee) with Jeg drikker aldrig kaffe (I never drink coffee). Do not add ikke (not) next to it.

sentence.da: Hun spiser **aldrig** kød.
sentence.en: She never eats meat.

alene.explanation: "Alene" means "alone" or "on your own". Compare Jeg bor alene (I live alone; nobody else is in my home) with Jeg er ensom (I feel lonely, which is a sad feeling).

sentence.da: Ingen er hjemme. Jeg er **alene**.
sentence.en: Nobody is home. I am alone.

alkohol.explanation: "Alkohol" means "alcohol". Danish does not put en (a) in front of it: Jeg drikker ikke alkohol (I do not drink alcohol). Alkoholfri øl means "alcohol-free beer".

sentence.da: Der er **alkohol** i øl og vin.
sentence.en: There is alcohol in beer and wine.

alle.explanation: "Alle" means "everyone" or "all". Alle sammen means "all together". Do not mix it up with alt (everything): Alt er her (Everything is here).

sentence.da: **Alle** børn er hjemme i dag.
sentence.en: All the children are home today.

allerede.explanation: "Allerede" means "already". Compare Han er her ikke endnu (He is not here yet) with Han er allerede her (He is already here, earlier than expected). For example, Jeg har allerede spist (I have already eaten).

sentence.da: Maden er **allerede** klar.
sentence.en: The food is already ready.

allergisk.explanation: "Allergisk" means "allergic". To say what you are allergic to, add over for (to / towards): Jeg er allergisk over for nødder (I am allergic to nuts).

sentence.da: Han er **allergisk** og kan ikke spise æg.
sentence.en: He is allergic and cannot eat eggs.

alligevel.explanation: "Alligevel" means "nevertheless" and "anyway". It shows something happens despite a problem: Det regner, men vi går alligevel (It is raining, but we are going anyway).

sentence.da: Jeg er træt, men jeg kommer **alligevel**.
sentence.en: I am tired, but I am coming anyway.

almindelig.explanation: "Almindelig" means "ordinary" or "common": normal, with nothing special about it. Det er en almindelig fejl (It is a common mistake).

sentence.da: Det var bare en **almindelig** dag på arbejde.
sentence.en: It was just an ordinary day at work.

alt.explanation: "Alt" means "everything" or "all". Compare Alle er her (Everyone is here) with Alt er her (Everything is here). Alt for means "far too": alt for dyrt (far too expensive).

sentence.da: Jeg har glemt **alt**.
sentence.en: I have forgotten everything.

alt i alt.explanation: "Alt i alt" means "all in all" and sums up what you have said: Alt i alt var det en god dag (All in all it was a good day). It usually comes at the end, after the details.

forms.da: Alt i alt går det godt.
forms.en: All in all it is going well.

sentence.da: **Alt i alt** var rejsen rigtig god.
sentence.en: All in all the trip was really good.

altid.explanation: "Altid" means "always", every single time, with no exceptions. Compare Jeg er aldrig træt (I am never tired) with Jeg er altid træt (I am always tired).

sentence.da: Jeg står **altid** op klokken seks.
sentence.en: I always get up at six o'clock.

alting.explanation: "Alting" means "everything": Alting er dyrt her (Everything is expensive here). It often appears with ikke: Ikke alting er dyrt (Not everything is expensive).

sentence.da: Hun ved **alting** om heste.
sentence.en: She knows everything about horses.

altså.explanation: "Altså" means "so" or "then", when you sum up what was just said: Han er syg, så han kommer altså ikke (He is sick, so he is not coming then). It also adds emphasis, like the English word really. Compare Det er dyrt (It is expensive) with Det er altså dyrt! (It really is expensive!).

sentence.da: Nu skal du **altså** gå i seng!
sentence.en: Now you really have to go to bed!

alvor.explanation: "Alvor" means "seriousness". You often use it in the phrase i alvor (seriously): Er du i alvor? (Are you serious?). It is the opposite of a joke: Nu er det alvor (Now it is serious).

sentence.da: Jeg mener det i fuldt **alvor**.
sentence.en: I mean it in all seriousness.

alvorlig.explanation: "Alvorlig" means "serious", for problems and for people: Det er en alvorlig sag (It is a serious matter). Han ser alvorlig ud (He looks serious).

sentence.da: Lægen siger, at det er en **alvorlig** sygdom.
sentence.en: The doctor says that it is a serious illness.

ambitiøs.explanation: "Ambitiøs" means "ambitious" and describes a person or a goal that aims high: Hun er ambitiøs på jobbet (She is ambitious at work).

sentence.da: Hun er **ambitiøs** og vil være chef en dag.
sentence.en: She is ambitious and wants to be a boss one day.

amerikansk.explanation: "Amerikansk" means "American", used for things from the USA. It is written with a small letter, while the English word American has a capital letter.

sentence.da: Burgere er **amerikansk** mad.
sentence.en: Burgers are American food.

anden.explanation: "Anden" means "second" and also "other". Compare min første dag (my first day) with min anden dag (my second day). Den anden bil can mean "the second car" or "the other car", and the situation tells you which. In dates: den anden juni (the second of June).

sentence.da: I dag er min **anden** dag her.
sentence.en: Today is my second day here.

anderledes.explanation: "Anderledes" means "different", as in not the usual way: Det er en anderledes film (It is a different kind of film). For things that are not alike, forskellig is common: De er forskellige (They are different).

sentence.da: Min nye skole er helt **anderledes**, ikke som den gamle.
sentence.en: My new school is completely different, not like the old one.

ansvarlig.explanation: "Ansvarlig" means "responsible" and describes someone you can rely on: Han er ansvarlig og kommer til tiden (He is responsible and comes on time). It also means in charge: Hvem er ansvarlig? (Who is in charge?)

sentence.da: Hun er **ansvarlig** og passer godt på sin lillebror.
sentence.en: She is responsible and takes good care of her little brother.

antibiotika.explanation: "Antibiotika" means "antibiotics" and is used without en or et, like in English: Hun får antibiotika (She is getting antibiotics). It only works against bacteria, not viruses: Det virker ikke mod virus (It does not work against viruses).

sentence.da: Lægen giver mig **antibiotika** mod infektionen.
sentence.en: The doctor gives me antibiotics for the infection.

appelsinjuice.explanation: "En appelsinjuice" means "an orange juice". It is built from appelsin (orange) and juice (juice). Et glas appelsinjuice means "a glass of orange juice".

sentence.da: **Appelsinjuice** er en sød drik lavet af appelsiner.
sentence.en: Orange juice is a sweet drink made from oranges.

appetit.explanation: "Appetit" means "appetite", the wish to eat: Jeg har ikke så meget appetit i dag (I don't have much appetite today). Lugten af nybagt brød giver mig appetit (The smell of fresh bread gives me an appetite).

sentence.da: Efter turen havde vi stor **appetit**.
sentence.en: After the trip we had a big appetite.

april.explanation: "April" means "April". Danish writes month names with a small letter, where English has a capital: i april (in April). Aprilsnar means "April fool", built from april and nar (fool).

sentence.da: Efter marts kommer **april**.
sentence.en: After March comes April.

arabisk.explanation: "Arabisk" means "Arabic", and it is used for the language and for things from the Arab world. It is written with a small letter, while the English word Arabic has a capital letter: Hun taler arabisk (She speaks Arabic).

sentence.da: Hun kommer fra Egypten og taler **arabisk**.
sentence.en: She comes from Egypt and speaks Arabic.

arbejdsløs.explanation: "Arbejdsløs" means "unemployed", without a job: Han har været arbejdsløs i et år (He has been unemployed for a year). It is built from arbejde (work) and løs (without).

sentence.da: Han har været **arbejdsløs** i tre måneder.
sentence.en: He has been unemployed for three months.

asiatisk.explanation: "Asiatisk" means "Asian" and describes things from Asia: asiatisk mad (Asian food). A person from Asia is en asiat (an Asian person).

sentence.da: Kina er et **asiatisk** land.
sentence.en: China is an Asian country.

asien.explanation: "Asien" means "Asia", the largest continent in the world: Hun har rejst meget i Asien (She has traveled a lot in Asia).

sentence.da: Kina og Japan ligger i **Asien**.
sentence.en: China and Japan are in Asia.

assistance.explanation: "Assistance" means "assistance", help from someone: Jeg har brug for assistance (I need assistance). It sounds more formal than hjælp (help).

sentence.da: Kan jeg få **assistance** ved kassen?
sentence.en: Can I get assistance at the checkout?

at acceptere.explanation: "At acceptere" means "to accept": Jeg accepterer dit tilbud (I accept your offer). It also fits things you must live with: Hun kan ikke acceptere, at han er sen (She cannot accept that he is late).

sentence.da: Du kan **acceptere** eller sige nej til jobbet.
sentence.en: You can accept or say no to the job.

at advare.explanation: "At advare" means "to warn", telling someone about a danger: Jeg advarer dig mod hunden (I am warning you about the dog). The danger comes after mod (against).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **advare** dig mod den glatte vej.
sentence.en: I want to warn you about the slippery road.

at afbestille.explanation: "At afbestille" means "to cancel" something you ordered or booked: Jeg afbestiller hotelværelset (I cancel the hotel room). For an event that will not happen, use at aflyse (to call off).

forms.en: I have canceled (an order or booking)

sentence.da: Vi må **afbestille** bordet, fordi Anna er syg.
sentence.en: We have to cancel the table because Anna is sick.

at afhænge af.explanation: "At afhænge af" means "to depend on": Det afhænger af vejret (It depends on the weather). In everyday speech, Danes often say det kommer an på (it depends on) instead.

sentence.da: Prisen vil **afhænge af** størrelsen.
sentence.en: The price will depend on the size.

at aflevere.explanation: "At aflevere" means "to hand in" and "to deliver": Jeg afleverer opgaven i morgen (I hand in the assignment tomorrow). It also means "to drop off": Jeg afleverer børnene i skole (I drop the kids off at school).

sentence.da: Du skal **aflevere** rapporten før fredag.
sentence.en: You have to hand in the report before Friday.

at aflyse.explanation: "At aflyse" means "to cancel", for an event, a flight or a meeting that will not happen: Flyet bliver aflyst (The flight is being canceled). For your own booking, use at afbestille (to cancel an order).

sentence.da: De må **aflyse** mødet på grund af sne.
sentence.en: They have to cancel the meeting because of snow.

at afslutte.explanation: "At afslutte" means "to finish" or "to end" something on purpose: Hun afsluttede brevet (She finished the letter). When something ends by itself, use at slutte: Filmen slutter nu (The film ends now).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **afslutte** rapporten i dag.
sentence.en: I have to finish the report today.

at aftale.explanation: "At aftale" means "to agree on" or "to arrange": two people settle a time or a plan together. Jeg har aftalt en tid med lægen (I have set a time with the doctor). The result is called en aftale (an agreement, an appointment).

sentence.da: Vi skal **aftale** en tid for mødet.
sentence.en: We have to arrange a time for the meeting.

at anbefale.explanation: "At anbefale" means "to recommend", for things you like and trust: Jeg anbefaler restauranten (I recommend the restaurant). It also works for advice about what to do: Lægen anbefaler hvile (The doctor recommends rest).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **anbefale** denne gode bog til dig.
sentence.en: I would like to recommend this good book to you.

at angre.explanation: "At angre" means "to regret": Jeg angrer, at jeg sagde det (I regret that I said it). It is about something you did or chose and wish you had not.

sentence.da: Du vil ikke **angre**, at du kom.
sentence.en: You will not regret that you came.

at ankomme.explanation: "At ankomme" means "to arrive", for trains, planes and guests: Gæsterne ankommer i dag (The guests arrive today). In everyday talk, Danes often say at komme frem (to get there).

sentence.da: Flyet skal **ankomme** klokken otte i aften.
sentence.en: The plane is due to arrive at eight tonight.

at ansætte.explanation: "At ansætte" means "to hire": Firmaet ansætter to nye folk (The company is hiring two new people). It means giving someone a job, not looking for one.

sentence.da: Vi vil gerne **ansætte** en ny kollega.
sentence.en: We would like to hire a new colleague.

at arbejde.explanation: "At arbejde" means "to work": Jeg arbejder på et hospital (I work at a hospital). Et arbejde also means "a job" or "work" itself: Jeg har meget arbejde (I have a lot of work).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **arbejde** på kontoret.
sentence.en: I have to work at the office.

at arbejde hjemmefra.explanation: "At arbejde hjemmefra" means "to work from home". Hjemmefra (from home) is one word: Jeg arbejder hjemmefra om fredagen (I work from home on Fridays). It is built from hjemme (at home) and fra (from).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **arbejde hjemmefra** på mandag.
sentence.en: I can work from home on Monday.

at arbejde med.explanation: "At arbejde med" means "to work with", and also to work in a field: Hun arbejder med dyr (She works with animals). For a place or a task, use på instead: Jeg arbejder på kontoret (I work at the office).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **arbejde med** børn.
sentence.en: I would like to work with children.

at arbejde på.explanation: "At arbejde på" means "to work at" a place, or "to work on" a task: Jeg arbejder på et hospital (I work at a hospital). Hun arbejder på et nyt projekt (She is working on a new project).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **arbejde på** min rapport i aften.
sentence.en: I want to work on my report tonight.

atten.explanation: "Atten" means "eighteen". Count with it: sytten, atten, nitten (seventeen, eighteen, nineteen). For age: Jeg er atten år (I am eighteen years old).

sentence.da: Min søn er **atten** år.
sentence.en: My son is eighteen years old.

august.explanation: "August" means "August". Danish writes month names with a small letter, so you write i august (in August), not i August.

sentence.da: Skolen starter igen i **august**.
sentence.en: School starts again in August.

australien.explanation: "Australien" means "Australia". Use i (in) for being there and til (to) for going there: Jeg bor i Australien (I live in Australia), Jeg rejser til Australien (I am traveling to Australia).

sentence.da: Kænguruer bor i **Australien**.
sentence.en: Kangaroos live in Australia.

automatisk.explanation: "Automatisk" means "automatic", something that happens by itself. The same word also tells how something happens: Døren åbner automatisk (The door opens automatically).

sentence.da: Lyset tændes **automatisk**, når du går ind.
sentence.en: The light comes on automatically when you walk in.

av.explanation: "Av" means "ouch" and is what you say when something hurts: Av, min fod! (Ouch, my foot!). For a small slip, say ups (oops) instead.

sentence.da: **Av**, den kop er varm!
sentence.en: Ouch, that cup is hot!

en abe.explanation: "En abe" means "a monkey", and also "an ape": Aben spiser en banan (The monkey eats a banana). For a great ape, Danes say en menneskeabe (a great ape).

sentence.da: En **abe** klatrer op i det høje træ.
sentence.en: A monkey climbs up the tall tree.

en abrikos.explanation: "En abrikos" means "an apricot", a small orange fruit with a large pit. Dried ones are a common snack: Jeg spiser tørrede abrikoser (I eat dried apricots).

sentence.da: En **abrikos** er lille og orange.
sentence.en: An apricot is small and orange.

en adgangskode.explanation: "En adgangskode" means "a password", a secret code that lets you in: Skriv din adgangskode to gange (Type your password twice). It is built from adgang (access) and kode (code).

sentence.da: Jeg har glemt min **adgangskode**.
sentence.en: I have forgotten my password.

en adresse.explanation: "En adresse" means "an address", the street and number where someone lives. You ask Hvad er din adresse? (What is your address?).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver min **adresse** på brevet: Vestergade 12.
sentence.en: I write my address on the letter: Vestergade 12.

en advarsel.explanation: "En advarsel" means "a warning", a message that danger or trouble may come: Læreren gav ham en advarsel (The teacher gave him a warning).

sentence.da: Der er en **advarsel** om kraftig regn i dag.
sentence.en: There is a warning about heavy rain today.

en advokat.explanation: "En advokat" means "a lawyer", someone who gives legal advice and speaks for you in court: Jeg har brug for en advokat (I need a lawyer). The same word is used for men and women.

sentence.da: Jeg ringer til en **advokat**, fordi jeg har en retssag.
sentence.en: I am calling a lawyer because I have a court case.

en afdeling.explanation: "En afdeling" means "a department", a part of a company, hospital or store: Min ven arbejder på en afdeling på hospitalet (My friend works in a department at the hospital).

sentence.da: Banken har en **afdeling** for lån.
sentence.en: The bank has a department for loans.

en afgang.explanation: "En afgang" means "a departure", the time a train, bus or plane leaves. You can ask Hvornår er næste afgang? (When is the next departure?).

sentence.da: Næste **afgang** er klokken ni.
sentence.en: The next departure is at nine.

en afkørsel.explanation: "En afkørsel" means "an exit" from a highway: Tag næste afkørsel (Take the next exit). For the exit of a building, use udgang (exit) instead.

sentence.da: Tag næste **afkørsel** og drej til højre.
sentence.en: Take the next exit and turn right.

en aflevering.explanation: "En aflevering" means "a submission", a piece of schoolwork you hand in: Jeg har en aflevering i morgen (I have a submission due tomorrow). It is also used for handing something over: aflevering af nøgler (handing over keys).

sentence.da: Jeg skal skrive min **aflevering** færdig i aften.
sentence.en: I have to finish writing my submission tonight.

en aflysning.explanation: "En aflysning" means "a cancellation" of something planned, like a flight or a match: Aflysningen skyldes dårligt vejr (The cancellation is due to bad weather). Vi fik besked om aflysningen (We were told about the cancellation).

sentence.da: Der kom en **aflysning** af flyet på grund af stormen.
sentence.en: There was a cancellation of the flight because of the storm.

en afrejse.explanation: "En afrejse" means "a departure", the moment you set off on a trip, often abroad. For a train or bus leaving a station, use afgang (departure) instead.

sentence.da: Vores **afrejse** er tidligt på fredag.
sentence.en: Our departure is early on Friday.

en afsked.explanation: "En afsked" means "a farewell" or "a goodbye", the moment you part, often for a long time: Det var en svær afsked (It was a hard goodbye). It is the parting itself, not the word you say when leaving.

sentence.da: Vi tog **afsked** på stationen.
sentence.en: We said goodbye at the station.

en afslutning.explanation: "En afslutning" means "an ending" or "a conclusion", the last part of something: Talen fik en god afslutning (The speech got a good ending).

sentence.da: Jeg kan godt lide filmens **afslutning**.
sentence.en: I like the ending of the film.

en afstand.explanation: "En afstand" means "a distance", the space between two places or people, measured in meters or kilometers. Hold afstand! means "Keep your distance!"

sentence.da: Der er en **afstand** på to kilometer til byen.
sentence.en: There is a distance of two kilometers to the town.

en aftale.explanation: "En aftale" means "an appointment" or "an agreement". An appointment: en aftale med tandlægen (an appointment with the dentist). A deal: Det er en aftale! (It's a deal!).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **aftale** med lægen.
sentence.en: I have an appointment with the doctor.

en aften.explanation: "En aften" means "an evening", the time of day between afternoon and night. Useful phrases are i aften (tonight), om aftenen (in the evening, as a habit), and god aften (good evening).

sentence.da: Vi spiser mad hver **aften**.
sentence.en: We eat dinner every evening.

en aftenrutine.explanation: "En aftenrutine" means "an evening routine", the things you do each night before bed: Først børster jeg tænder, så læser jeg lidt (First I brush my teeth, then I read a bit).

sentence.da: Min **aftenrutine** er te, en bog og tidlig seng.
sentence.en: My evening routine is tea, a book and an early bed.

en aftentur.explanation: "En aftentur" means "an evening walk", a calm walk after dinner: Vi tager en aftentur (We take an evening walk). It is built from aften (evening) and tur (walk, trip).

sentence.da: Efter maden tager vi en **aftentur** langs vandet.
sentence.en: After dinner we take an evening walk along the water.

en agurk.explanation: "En agurk" means "a cucumber", a long, green vegetable that is crisp and watery. Pickled ones are syltede agurker (pickled cucumbers).

sentence.da: Jeg skærer en **agurk** til salaten.
sentence.en: I am cutting a cucumber for the salad.

en airbag.explanation: "En airbag" means "an airbag", the cushion that fills with air in a crash: Bilen har fire airbags (The car has four airbags). Airbagen går af, hvis bilen rammer noget (The airbag goes off if the car hits something).

sentence.da: Min nye bil har en **airbag** i rattet.
sentence.en: My new car has an airbag in the steering wheel.

en airfryer.explanation: "En airfryer" means "an air fryer", a small oven that cooks with hot air and little oil, so food turns crispy: Jeg bruger airfryeren til kylling (I use the air fryer for chicken).

sentence.da: Man kan lave pommes frites i en **airfryer**.
sentence.en: You can make fries in an air fryer.

en aktivitet.explanation: "En aktivitet" means "an activity", something you do for fun or exercise, like hiking or board games. It is also used for planned events at a school or club: aktiviteter for børn (activities for children).

sentence.da: Svømning er en sjov **aktivitet** for hele familien.
sentence.en: Swimming is a fun activity for the whole family.

en akvariefisk.explanation: "En akvariefisk" means "an aquarium fish", a fish kept at home in a tank. It is built from akvarium (aquarium) and fisk (fish). Jeg har tre akvariefisk (I have three aquarium fish).

sentence.da: En **akvariefisk** lever i et akvarium med planter.
sentence.en: An aquarium fish lives in an aquarium with plants.

en alarm.explanation: "En alarm" means "an alarm", both a warning sound and the wake-up alarm on a phone: Alarmen gik i nat (The alarm went off last night). To turn it off, say Jeg slukker alarmen (I turn off the alarm).

sentence.da: Min **alarm** ringer klokken seks hver morgen.
sentence.en: My alarm rings at six every morning.

en alarmklokke.explanation: "En alarmklokke" means "an alarm bell", a bell that rings to warn people: Alarmklokken ringer (The alarm bell is ringing). It is built from alarm (alarm) and klokke (bell).

sentence.da: Vi hørte en **alarmklokke** ringe midt om natten.
sentence.en: We heard an alarm bell ring in the middle of the night.

en albue.explanation: "En albue" means "an elbow". Danish often says the elbow where English says my elbow: Jeg har slået albuen is literally I have hit the elbow, meaning "I have hit my elbow". Min albue is also fine.

sentence.da: Armen bøjer ved din **albue**.
sentence.en: The arm bends at your elbow.

en alder.explanation: "En alder" means "an age", how old someone is. To ask, Danes say Hvor gammel er du? (How old are you?), because alder sounds formal, like on a form. You will also see it in i min alder (at my age).

sentence.da: På blanketten skal du skrive din **alder**.
sentence.en: On the form, you have to write your age.

en allergi.explanation: "En allergi" means "an allergy", when your body reacts badly to something like nuts, pollen or cats. In compounds it comes last: en pollenallergi (a pollen allergy).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **allergi** mod nødder.
sentence.en: I have an allergy to nuts.

en altan.explanation: "En altan" means "a balcony", the small outdoor space attached to an apartment: Vi drikker kaffe på altanen (We drink coffee on the balcony).

sentence.da: Vi sidder på vores **altan** og nyder solen.
sentence.en: We sit on our balcony and enjoy the sun.

en ambassade.explanation: "En ambassade" means "an embassy", one country's office in another country: Den danske ambassade ligger i Berlin (The Danish embassy is in Berlin). Du kan få hjælp på ambassaden (You can get help at the embassy).

sentence.da: Vi fik hjælp fra den danske **ambassade** i Rom.
sentence.en: We got help from the Danish embassy in Rome.

en ambulance.explanation: "En ambulance" means "an ambulance", a vehicle that takes sick or hurt people to the hospital. In an emergency in Denmark, you call 112.

sentence.da: Han er meget syg. Ring efter en **ambulance**!
sentence.en: He is very sick. Call for an ambulance!

en amerikaner.explanation: "En amerikaner" means "an American", a person from the USA, used for both men and women. It does not start with a capital letter: Hun er amerikaner (She is an American).

sentence.da: Hun er **amerikaner** og bor i Danmark.
sentence.en: She is American and lives in Denmark.

en ananas.explanation: "En ananas" means "a pineapple", a tropical fruit with a rough, spiky skin and juicy flesh. Pineapple juice is ananasjuice (pineapple juice).

sentence.da: En **ananas** er sød og gul indeni.
sentence.en: A pineapple is sweet and yellow inside.

en anbefaling.explanation: "En anbefaling" means "a recommendation", advice about what is good: Tak for anbefalingen (Thanks for the recommendation). Doctors give them too: lægens anbefaling (the doctor's recommendation).

sentence.da: Tak for din **anbefaling** af den restaurant.
sentence.en: Thanks for your recommendation of that restaurant.

en and.explanation: "En and" means "a duck". Watch out: anden also means "the other" or "second", as in den anden (the other one), so the rest of the sentence shows which is meant.

sentence.da: En **and** svømmer på søen.
sentence.en: A duck is swimming on the lake.

en ankomst.explanation: "En ankomst" means "an arrival", the time a train, plane or person gets somewhere: Hvornår er ankomsten? (When is the arrival?).

sentence.da: Vores **ankomst** er klokken tolv.
sentence.en: Our arrival is at twelve.

en ankomsthal.explanation: "En ankomsthal" means "an arrivals hall", the area in an airport where arriving passengers come out and meet people: Jeg venter i ankomsthallen (I wait in the arrivals hall). It is built from ankomst (arrival) and hal (hall).

sentence.da: Passagererne kommer ud i en **ankomsthal** efter landingen.
sentence.en: The passengers come out into an arrivals hall after landing.

en annonce.explanation: "En annonce" means "an advertisement", in a paper or online: en annonce for et job (an ad for a job). A TV or radio ad is usually en reklame (a commercial).

sentence.da: Jeg så en **annonce** for en ny telefon.
sentence.en: I saw an ad for a new phone.

en ansat.explanation: "En ansat" means "an employee", a person who works for a company: Der er tyve ansatte her (There are twenty employees here). Jeg er ansat her (I am employed here) uses the same word.

sentence.da: Hver **ansat** får en ny telefon.
sentence.en: Every employee gets a new phone.

en ansigtscreme.explanation: "En ansigtscreme" means "a face cream", a cream that keeps your skin soft. It is built from ansigt (face) and creme (cream).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger **ansigtscreme** hver morgen, fordi min hud er tør.
sentence.en: I use face cream every morning because my skin is dry.

en ansøgning.explanation: "En ansøgning" means "an application", a letter asking for something: en ansøgning om et job (an application for a job). You write it: Jeg skriver en ansøgning (I am writing an application).

sentence.da: Jeg har sendt min **ansøgning** til firmaet.
sentence.en: I have sent my application to the company.

en app.explanation: "En app" means "an app", a small program on your phone or tablet. To download one, Danes say at hente en app (literally to fetch an app), and to open it, at åbne appen (to open the app).

sentence.da: Jeg henter en **app** til min telefon.
sentence.en: I am downloading an app for my phone.

en appelsin.explanation: "En appelsin" means "an orange", the fruit. English uses "orange" for both fruit and color, but Danish has two words: appelsin for the fruit and orange for the color, as in en orange bold (an orange ball).

sentence.da: Af en **appelsin** kan man presse juice.
sentence.en: You can squeeze juice from an orange.

en arbejdsdag.explanation: "En arbejdsdag" means "a working day", a day when you work from start to finish: Det var en lang arbejdsdag (It was a long workday). The opposite is en fridag (a day off).

sentence.da: Min **arbejdsdag** slutter klokken fire.
sentence.en: My working day ends at four o'clock.

en arbejdsgiver.explanation: "En arbejdsgiver" means "an employer", the person or company you work for. It is built from arbejde (work) and at give (to give): the one who gives you work. Min arbejdsgiver er et stort firma (My employer is a big company).

sentence.da: Min **arbejdsgiver** betaler for kurset.
sentence.en: My employer pays for the course.

en arbejdsplads.explanation: "En arbejdsplads" means "a workplace", the place where you work: Min arbejdsplads ligger i centrum (My workplace is in the center). It is built from arbejde (work) and plads (place).

sentence.da: Jeg ser mine kolleger på min **arbejdsplads**.
sentence.en: I see my colleagues at my workplace.

en arkitekt.explanation: "En arkitekt" means "an architect", a person who designs buildings and plans how they will look: Hun har tegnet vores nye skole (She designed our new school). It is used for both men and women.

sentence.da: Min søster er **arkitekt** og tegner huse.
sentence.en: My sister is an architect and draws houses.

en arm.explanation: "En arm" means "an arm". Danish often says the arm where English says her arm: Hun har brækket armen is literally She has broken the arm, meaning "She has broken her arm".

sentence.da: Hånden sidder for enden af din **arm**.
sentence.en: Your hand is at the end of your arm.

en artikel.explanation: "En artikel" means "an article", a piece of writing in a paper or on a website: Jeg læste en artikel om rejser (I read an article about travel). For an item in a shop, use en vare (a product).

sentence.da: Jeg læste en **artikel** om vores by.
sentence.en: I read an article about our city.

en assistent.explanation: "En assistent" means "an assistant", a person who helps with the work: Assistenten svarer på mails (The assistant answers emails).

sentence.da: Min **assistent** skriver mails til kunderne.
sentence.en: My assistant writes emails to the customers.

en astronaut.explanation: "En astronaut" means "an astronaut", a person who travels into space: Astronauten fløj til månen (The astronaut flew to the moon).

sentence.da: En **astronaut** rejser i en raket til månen.
sentence.en: An astronaut travels in a rocket to the moon.

en aubergine.explanation: "En aubergine" means "an eggplant". You usually cook it before eating it: Jeg bager en aubergine i ovnen (I bake an eggplant in the oven).

sentence.da: En **aubergine** er en lilla grønsag.
sentence.en: An eggplant is a purple vegetable.

en autograf.explanation: "En autograf" means "an autograph", a famous person's signature: Jeg fik en autograf af skuespilleren (I got an autograph from the actor). To ask for one, say Må jeg få en autograf? (May I have an autograph?)

sentence.da: Jeg fik en **autograf** af min yndlingssanger.
sentence.en: I got an autograph from my favorite singer.

en autostol.explanation: "En autostol" means "a car seat", the safety seat for a child in a car: Barnet sidder i autostolen (The child sits in the car seat). It is built from auto (car) and stol (chair).

sentence.da: Barnet skal sidde i en **autostol** i bilen.
sentence.en: The child has to sit in a car seat in the car.

en avis.explanation: "En avis" means "a newspaper", printed pages with the day's news. At læse avisen means "to read the paper". Do not mix it up with et blad (a magazine).

sentence.da: Min far læser en **avis** hver morgen.
sentence.en: My dad reads a newspaper every morning.

en avocado.explanation: "En avocado" means "an avocado". To see if it is ready, press it: Er den blød, er den moden (If it is soft, it is ripe).

sentence.da: Guacamole er lavet af **avocado**.
sentence.en: Guacamole is made of avocado.

et abonnement.explanation: "Et abonnement" means "a subscription", something you pay for again and again to keep getting a service: Jeg har et abonnement på et magasin (I have a subscription to a magazine).

sentence.da: Jeg betaler hver måned for mit **abonnement**.
sentence.en: I pay for my subscription every month.

et afsnit.explanation: "Et afsnit" means "an episode" of a show, and also a section of a text: Jeg har set tre afsnit (I have watched three episodes). For a TV show, en episode (an episode) means the same.

sentence.da: Vi så det sidste **afsnit** i går aftes.
sentence.en: We watched the last episode last night.

et akvarium.explanation: "Et akvarium" means "an aquarium", a big glass tank with fish and other water animals, or a place with many tanks: Vi så hajer i akvariet (We saw sharks in the aquarium).

sentence.da: Børnene kan se fisk i et stort **akvarium**.
sentence.en: The children can see fish in a big aquarium.

et alarmnummer.explanation: "Et alarmnummer" means "an emergency number", a phone number you call in danger: I Danmark er det 112 (In Denmark it is 112). Det er gratis at ringe til alarmnummeret (It is free to call the emergency number).

sentence.da: Du kan ringe til **alarmnummer** 112.
sentence.en: You can call the emergency number 112.

et album.explanation: "Et album" means "an album", most often for music: Hun har et nyt album (She has a new album). It is also used for photos: et fotoalbum (a photo album).

sentence.da: Bandet har lavet et nyt **album**.
sentence.en: The band has made a new album.

et alfabet.explanation: "Et alfabet" means "an alphabet", the set of letters a language is written with: Jeg kan hele alfabetet (I know the whole alphabet).

sentence.da: Æ, ø og å kommer sidst i det danske **alfabet**.
sentence.en: Æ, ø and å come last in the Danish alphabet.

et anker.explanation: "Et anker" means "an anchor", the heavy metal weight that keeps a boat in place: Skibet ligger for anker (The ship is at anchor). Ankeret trækkes op (The anchor is pulled up).

sentence.da: Kaptajnen kaster **anker** uden for havnen.
sentence.en: The captain drops anchor outside the harbor.

et ansigt.explanation: "Et ansigt" means "a face", the front of your head, where you smile and show how you feel. Vask dit ansigt (Wash your face), et glad ansigt (a happy face).

sentence.da: Øjne og næse sidder i dit **ansigt**.
sentence.en: Eyes and nose are in your face.

et ansvar.explanation: "Et ansvar" means "a responsibility", something you must take care of: Det er mit ansvar (It is my responsibility). To accept it, say at tage ansvar (to take responsibility).

sentence.da: Du har et stort **ansvar** på arbejdet.
sentence.en: You have a big responsibility at work.

et antal.explanation: "Et antal" means "a number" in the sense of how many: Antallet af elever er tyve (The number of students is twenty). For the number 5 itself, use et tal (a number).

sentence.da: Et stort **antal** mennesker kom til festen.
sentence.en: A large number of people came to the party.

et apotek.explanation: "Et apotek" means "a pharmacy", the shop where you buy medicine. The person working there is en farmaceut (a pharmacist). Say på apoteket for "at the pharmacy".

sentence.da: Jeg køber medicin på et **apotek**.
sentence.en: I buy medicine at a pharmacy.

et apparat.explanation: "Et apparat" means "a device" or "an appliance", something you plug in and use: Vi har mange apparater i køkkenet (We have many appliances in the kitchen).

sentence.da: Det nye **apparat** i køkkenet er meget let at bruge.
sentence.en: The new appliance in the kitchen is very easy to use.

et arbejde.explanation: "Et arbejde" means "a job" or "work". Danes say på arbejde (at work): Jeg er på arbejde means "I am at work", and "at gå på arbejde" means "to go to work".

sentence.da: Jeg skal på **arbejde** nu.
sentence.en: I have to go to work now.

et argument.explanation: "Et argument" means "an argument", a reason you give for your view: Det er et stærkt argument (That is a strong argument). For a quarrel, use et skænderi (a quarrel).

sentence.da: Jeg har et godt **argument** for at blive hjemme.
sentence.en: I have a good argument for staying home.

et armbånd.explanation: "Et armbånd" means "a bracelet". It is built from arm (arm) and bånd (band): Han gav hende et armbånd (He gave her a bracelet).

sentence.da: Hun har et pænt **armbånd** om håndleddet.
sentence.en: She has a pretty bracelet around her wrist.

et askebæger.explanation: "Et askebæger" means "an ashtray". It is built from aske (ash) and bæger (cup): Der står et askebæger på bordet (There is an ashtray on the table).

sentence.da: Hun lægger cigaretten i et **askebæger**.
sentence.en: She puts the cigarette in an ashtray.

et autoværksted.explanation: "Et autoværksted" means "a car repair shop", where mechanics fix cars. It is built from auto (car) and et værksted (a workshop): Bilen er på autoværkstedet i dag (The car is at the car repair shop today).

sentence.da: Bilen er i stykker, og jeg skal til et **autoværksted**.
sentence.en: The car is broken, and I have to go to a car repair shop.
